items.text: Description: Exponential backoff implementation for rate-limited marketplace APIs.
Keywords: exponential backoff, rate limit, delay, jitter
Exponential backoff applies to rate-limited responses (HTTP 429).
Backoff delay is multiplied by 2 each attempt.
Backoff adds random jitter to prevent thundering herd.
Backoff has no agent involvement — purely automatic.
Exponential backoff handles Amazon rate limiting gracefully.
Exponential backoff handles Flipkart rate limiting gracefully.
Description: Per-marketplace rate limiting to respect API quotas.
Keywords: rate limiting, throttling, API quota, marketplace
Each marketplace adapter implements its own rate limiter.
Each adapter's rate limiter is based on the marketplace's published API quotas.
Queued requests are dispatched within rate limits.
If rate limits are exceeded, exponential backoff applies.
Rate limit metrics are tracked for observability.
Description: How marketplace API throttling is managed per-account.
Bounded concurrency per marketplace account ensures we never exceed API limits.
Each marketplace adapter maintains a semaphore/token bucket.
The semaphore/token bucket controls how many concurrent API calls are in flight.
Bounded concurrency prevents mass bulk operations from triggering account-level throttling.
Description: Idempotency keys on all marketplace mutations.
Keywords: idempotency, keys, double publish, deduplication
Marketplace-mutation idempotency is labelled an Invariant.
Every marketplace write operation includes an idempotency key.
If a network failure causes uncertainty about whether a publish succeeded, retrying with the same key is safe.
Retrying with the same idempotency key is safe because the marketplace will deduplicate.
Page [137] Partial Failure Handling scope: MVP.
Description: Handling partial marketplace success — retry only failed fields.
Keywords: partial failure, partial success, field-level retry
Partial-failure field-level retry is labelled an Invariant.
On partial API success, retry only failed fields.
Never re-push the whole listing on partial API success.
The adapter's ListingResult tells exactly which fields succeeded.
The adapter's ListingResult tells exactly which fields failed.
Field-level retry prevents overwriting already-successful fields.
Field-level retry reduces unnecessary API calls.
Page [138] Dead Letter / Failed Jobs scope: MVP.
Description: How permanently failed jobs are handled — dead letter queue and reprocessing.
Keywords: dead letter, failed jobs, reprocessing, DLQ
Jobs that exhaust all retry attempts are moved to a dead letter queue.
Each failed job preserves its full ErrorReport.
Each failed job preserves its input context.
Each failed job preserves its failure history.
Description: How failed jobs can be retried with the same input.
Keywords: reprocessing, retry, failed jobs, re-run
Every AgentRun stores its complete input.
Failed jobs can be re-submitted with the same input.
Re-submission creates a new AgentRun with the same context.
Job reprocessing enables debugging and recovery without data loss.
Description: CSV bulk import batch processing — row-level validation, fan-out, aggregate results.
Keywords: batch, processing, bulk, CSV, fan-out
Batch step 4: fan-out into parallel Agent Runs.
Partial failures isolate to the row.
The batch completes with a summary report.
Page [141] Parallel Agent Runs scope: MVP.
Description: How multiple agents and multiple products are processed in parallel.
Keywords: parallel, agent runs, concurrency, bounded
Within a single listing generation: Content, Keyword, Attribute, and Image agents run in parallel.
Content, Keyword, Attribute, and Image agents have no inter-dependencies.
Across multiple products (bulk import): bounded concurrency limits how many products are processed simultaneously.
Description: Model routing architecture — cheapest model that meets quality bar.
Keywords: model routing, model selection, GPT-4o mini, DeepSeek, fallback, escalation
Core principle: use the cheapest model that meets the quality requirement.
The model is an abstraction, not a hardcoded dependency.
GPT-4o mini rationale: strong structured output.
Image compliance vision model: GPT-4o mini (vision).
Same model for text and images = simpler pipeline.
text-embedding-3-small rationale: adequate for cosine retrieval.
GPT-4o used only if mini fails repeated corrections.

Page [143] Model Selection Policy scope: MVP.
Description: Rules for selecting which model to use for each task.
Keywords: model selection, policy, rules, which model
Rule 1: Default route = GPT-4o mini for text + vision.
Selection rule 2: if output fails JSON validation twice → escalate to next tier (GPT-4o).
Selection rule 3: if task is text-only and budget-constrained → route to DeepSeek-V3.
Rule 4: Embeddings always use the embedding model.
Never run the generation model for retrieval.
Rule 5: Log model_used, tokens, and cost on every AgentRun.
Description: Fallback chain when primary model fails.
Keywords: fallback, model failure, escalation, backup
Fallback chain step 4: Escalate to GPT-4o.
Fallback chain step 5: if still failing, mark job as blocked.
Each fallback step is logged with cost.
Each fallback step is logged with duration.
The system never silently switches models.
Page [145] Heavy Reasoning Escalation scope: MVP.
Heavier models are more expensive; escalate to them for complex corrections.
Keywords: heavy reasoning, escalation, GPT-4o, complex
Escalate to the heavier model only when one of the listed escalation criteria holds.
Criterion: JSON output fails validation twice with mini.
Escalation criterion: semantic correction fails repeatedly (same error persists).
Escalation criterion: the task requires complex multi-constraint reasoning.
Other agent runs continue with the default model during an escalation.
Description: How AI JSON output is validated against Pydantic schemas.
Keywords: JSON validation, Pydantic, schema validation, structured
Every AI agent output is validated against a Pydantic schema.
The output schema defines required fields.
The output schema defines field types.
The output schema defines string constraints (max length).
The output schema defines value enumerations.
Invalid JSON triggers the repair pipeline.
Page [147] Structured Output Repair scope: MVP.
Description: How malformed AI output is repaired before escalating to a heavier model.
Keywords: output repair, fix JSON, malformed, repair
Repair step 1: parse error identification — what exactly is wrong with the JSON.
Programmatic fix handles missing closing brackets.
Repair step 3: re-prompt with error details.
Repair step 4: if still failing, escalate to heavier model.
Description: Token usage tracking, limits, and optimization.

Page [149] AI Cost Optimization scope: MVP.
Description: Strategies for minimizing AI costs — model routing, caching, avoiding unnecessary regeneration.
Keywords: cost optimization, AI cost, efficiency, savings
Model routing — Use cheapest model that meets quality bar.
Prompt compression — Minimize token usage in prompts.
Retrieval top-k: only retrieve most relevant brand chunks (top-k=8).
Avoid unnecessary regeneration: don't regenerate if only one field failed.
Event-driven generation: generate only when needed, not on schedule.
Reuse approved outputs: clone approved listings for similar products.
Image processing only when required: skip unchanged images.
Batch embeddings: batch embed multiple chunks in one API call.
Bounded retries: max 3 correction attempts, not unlimited.

Description: Multi-tenancy enforcement — tenant_id on every query at repository layer.
Tenant isolation is labelled an Invariant.
Every database query includes tenant_id filtering.
tenant_id filtering is enforced at the repository layer — not the application layer.
Cross-tenant data leakage is a critical security violation.
Tenant data isolation is enforced at the database level.
Keywords: tenant isolation, data isolation, repository layer
The tenant_id comes from the authenticated JWT.
The tenant_id cannot be overridden by the client.
Tenant filtering is implemented in a base repository class.
All entity repositories extend the base repository class.
Four roles: Owner, Operator, Reviewer, Admin.
Each API endpoint specifies required roles.
Authorization middleware checks JWT claims against endpoint requirements.
Maker-checker is enforced at the business logic layer.
